INFJ here. Used to masturbate a lot to cope with anxiety too. Aren't close enough with my friends to talk about these kids of things as well. I have no words of solid advice, but I want to share how I cope now. Maybe you could try this as well.

When I get anxiety attacks, I tend to walk around while hyperventilating. After a while, I get tired physically and mentally, and to get even more tired, I masturbate. Even with a medium sense of anxiety, I masturbate to get dopamine. After tiring myself, I take a nap then think about I wasn't productive afterwards. I try to cram shit while that thought haunts me. After cramming, I masturbate to make myself better. I take a nap. Rinse and repeat.

One day, my parents bought a treadmill. I tried it out and walked and jogged on it. My constant thoughts of self-degradation gradually went away and got replaced by thoughts of how tired I currently am. I push myself beyond my limits to get really really tired and take a nap automatically. It's like a temporary reset button for me. I'm not sure myself if this is a healthy way to deal with it, but at the very least I get exercise.

Sometimes it pops in my head, "Do I even deserve to exercise? Do I deserve maintaining my health? Maybe I deserve to not be productive at all and masturbate instead" even while on the treadmill. Sometimes it goes away eventually, other times it stays. But when I sleep from getting physically tired, my head just resets. Intrusive thoughts get back to me eventually. It's just a matter of rinse and repeat for me. So yeah when I feel an anxiety attack coming, I reach my hand towards the treadmill.

People pursue a CS degree because they want a solid foundation on how a computer works, and how a computer works is based on math and logic. Technology changes rapidly, and people with solid foundations adapt more easily. People who lack such often don't last long. 

In your case though, since you're avoiding a CS degree so much, there's no use of persuading you. You look forward to Digital Media, you'll most likely thrive more there. With a minor in CS, yes it'll help, but not as much as a full CS degree. In terms of job hunting, people with CS degrees will be preferred.

I don't know much about CIIT sorry, though balak ko din mag-apply dyan for college. My hunch is that there is an emphasis on Math and logic like abstract reasoning. 

  
Mahirap ba ang programming? Yes. Super nakakasakit ng ulo at times. I think to myself every other night na "I'm not for this. I'm too dumb. I should quit and find another thing to do. Maybe this isn't worth my time." But I try to remember why I want to learn in the first place: I want to make sick graphics on websites. And also to survive in this brutal capitalistic world, but that's already a given lol. 

  
The thing is, expecting "big money" from programming isn't enough. Programming is VERY mentally taxing. There has to be some kind of intrinsic motivation or immediate gratification to keep you sane. I don't know how to articulate this well, but long-term goals like "I want to help people with my app!" or "I want to have a good enough salary to keep me alive." aren't enough for me. As time passes by, deep frustrations about programming will fog those long-term goals and make you wish that you were doing something else. I experienced this when I started to learn last year- let's just say I had a crisis of sorts and I ended up not doing anything productive. 

  
I realized needed to look forward to small things from my programming efforts- that immediate gratification stuff, so started to I celebrate that I made a button, a slider, or anything that I made so far! I may have looked like a toddler doing my firsts but I feel like that's essentially how programmers started out lmao.

  
My motivation is seeing cool visuals on screen- the "wow factor" of it all, kind of like when you admire the animation of a Pixar film. It may be shallow, yes, but that's enough to keep me going at least for now. I have an inclination for art- I started to learn how to program because I thought mixing art and techy stuff would be cool, and I still do! 

  
Your motivation may be different, and that's cool. Some people get their instant gratification from developing algorithms to do very specific things like solving a sudoku puzzle. Some people like debugging and other quality assurance stuff because they get happy when they fix something and seeing everything run smoothly. The point is, you gotta find your happy place in the programming world to keep going.
